i.norm: Tests {@link UnsynchronizedByteArrayInputStream#read(byte[], int, int)}, the explicit offset/length read overload.
Creates a stream backed by the given bytes. The builder declares a checked {@link IOException}, but it can never be thrown here because no conversion is needed for an in-memory byte array.
An empty stream always reports end-of-stream and never touches the destination buffer, regardless of the requested offset/length window.
Requesting zero bytes reads nothing (returns 0) even when data is available.
Partial then remaining reads: a 3-byte stream read in chunks of 2 then up to 10.
First read: ask for 2 bytes, get the first 2 (0xa, 0xb); the rest of the buffer is untouched.
Second read: ask for up to 10 bytes, but only the final byte (0xc) remains.

Reads into a fresh 10-byte buffer from an empty stream and asserts that the read reports end-of-stream while leaving the buffer all-zeros. @param offset the destination offset passed to read. @param length the requested length passed to read.
